summary: Data Loading issue for TV/Radio Sponsorship
description:
Chad and I looked into this and this was our 
findings.



The blanks are appearing because the data loader doesn't seem 
to like instances of accents on characters and instances of '£' e.g. within
the TV sponsorship data, the 'e' within 'Citroën' was causing the programme
row to appear as blank. I created a quick SUBSTITUTE formula to remove any 
instances of these (see below)

> 
=SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(D2
,"é","e"),"ñ","n"),"ç","c"),"ü","u"),"\u00e
1","a"),"—","-"),"ë","e")

This proved that instances of 
'ë' , '—' were causing that cell to appear blank (the others were 
added just in case)

We loaded the data onto Live and fixed the accent 
character issue however we were unable to fix the '£' issue and Chad 
manually fixed the one row that had the issue.



When we moved over to 
Radio Sponsorship there were instances of the wrong ' being used so I updated 
the formula and that fixed the issue for some of them and then I individually 
checked the rows of data and it seems that the rows that were appearing blank 
all had issues with '£'



note: Chad noticed that within the database,
an instance of ' appears as &#039 in order to appear correctly within the 
database

![](image9.png){width=70%}

![](image10.png){width=70%}

Essenti
ally, is there something that could be done during the loading process for these
not to be ignored and entered as a blank on the report and allow all text into 
the 
database?

summary: Jicmail report in mapping - additional tooltips for headers
description:
**Total attention seconds**

Average attention in seconds 
for a piece of mail multiplied by the number of households in the post 
sector

 

**CPM £ (attention seconds)**

Total cost for sending
a piece of mail to the post sector divided by the total attention seconds, to 
get a cost per attention second, and then multiplying this by 1,000 to get the 
CPM.

 

**Impressions**

Average frequency for a piece of mail 
multiplied by the number of households in the post sector

 

**CPM 
£ (impressions)**

Total cost for sending a piece of mail to the post 
sector divided by the total impressions, to get a cost per impression, and then 
multiplying this by 1,000 to get the CPM.

 

**Total commercial 
actions**

Average number of commercial actions for a piece of mail multiplied
by the number of households in the post sector

 

**CPCA 
£**

Total cost for sending a piece of mail to the post sector divided by
the total commercial actions

Re-vamp Radio Sponsorship Report
description:
## **Summary**

This project delivers an enhanced **Radio 
Sponsorship reporting capability** that improves data accuracy, usability, and 
analytical value for end users by introducing new brand-level data, refined 
filtering controls, and improved report outputs.

---

## **Problem / 
Opportunity**

The current reporting approach:

* Does not fully support 
**brand-level visibility**, limiting depth of analysis across sponsorship 
activity. [\[Radio Spon...ck-up v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)
* Uses inconsistent or unclear terminology (e.g.
Programme vs Contents, Company vs Sponsor), reducing clarity for business users.
[\[Radio Spon...ck-up v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)
* Produces **large, repetitive datasets**, 
making it harder to extract meaningful insights quickly. [\[Radio Spon...ck-up 
v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)
* Has limited usability in filtering and 
selection, slowing down report creation and exploration. [\[Radio Spon...ck-up 
v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)

This creates inefficiencies in reporting, 
increases manual effort, and reduces the value that clients derive from 
sponsorship data.

---

## **Proposed Solution**

Enhance the Radio 
Sponsorship report by:

### 1. **Improved Data Model**

* Introduce a new 
**Brand data field** from Nielsen and structure it alongside Sponsor data. 
[\[Radio Spon...ck-up v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)
* Split and structure data to support meaningful
reporting (Brand vs Programme/Contents). [\[Radio Spon...ck-up v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)
* Align terminology to business language 
(Sponsor, Contents). [\[Radio Spon...ck-up v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)

### 2. **Advanced Filtering & Selection 
(LHM)**

* Provide flexible filtering for:
  * Date (with configurable range)
[\[Radio Spon...ck-up v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)
  * Station / Channel [\[Radio Spon...ck-up v1 1
\| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere

  * Sponsor and Brand (with hierarchy) [\[Radio

60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere

  * Programme and Franchise Area

  * Confirm-to-apply filtering

lists

60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere
direct=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)

### 3. **Enhanced Report Output**

* 
Provide:
  * Clear **result counts and pagination** for large datasets [\[Radio
Spon...ck-up v1 1 \| 
PowerPoint\]](https://adwantedintl-my.sharepoint.com/personal/graeme_smith_uk_a
dwanted_com/\_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B5EFC6F55-091E-4F7E-8CD6-A58310C0
60B2%7D&file=Radio%20Spon%20-%20LHM%20mock-up%20v1%201.pptx&action=edit&mobilere

summary:
tamar1: Docker build fails for php8med - lzma memory allocation 
error due to missing swapaccount kernel parameter
description:
## Problem

Building the `php8med` Docker image on 
**tamar1** (`/opt/docker`) fails with the following error during `apt-get 
install`:

```
dpkg-deb (subprocess): decompressing archive 
'...00-libexpat1_2.7.1-2_amd64.deb' member 'control.tar': lzma error: Cannot 
allocate memory
tar: This does not look like a tar archive
dpkg-deb: error: 
tar subprocess returned error exit status 2
...
E: Sub-process /usr/bin/dpkg 
returned an error code (1)
ERROR: Service 'php8med' failed to build
```

The
same build succeeds on **ukwebdev1** (test) and locally.

## Environment

- 
**Host**: tamar1 (AWS EC2 instance, EBS-backed, no local/instance store volumes,
no swap configured)
- **OS**: Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS (Xenial) — **EOL since 
April 2021**
- **Docker**: 20.10.7
- **RAM**: 30.97 GiB
- **Service 
affected**: php8med Docker build (`/opt/docker`)

## Root Cause

`docker 
info` on tamar1 shows:

```
Total Memory: 30.97GiB
WARNING: No swap limit 
support
```

The `No swap limit support` warning indicates the kernel is 
missing the `swapaccount=1` boot parameter. However, since tamar1 is an AWS 
instance with **no swap configured**, this warning is largely cosmetic and the 
GRUB parameter change would have limited impact.

The actual cause of the 
`lzma: Cannot allocate memory` error with 30GB of available RAM is most likely 
**restrictive ulimits or Docker daemon defaults** on the instance. Modern `.deb`
packages (Debian Trixie era — e.g. cmake 3.31.6, libexpat 2.7.1) use 
high-compression xz/lzma, which requires significant memory to decompress and is
sensitive to ulimit or cgroup restrictions inside the build container.

### 
Diagnostic Commands

Run these on tamar1 to confirm:

```bash
# Check 
Docker daemon config for ulimit or memory restrictions
cat 
/etc/docker/daemon.json

# Check active ulimits inside a container (compare 
with host)
docker run --rm debian:bookworm bash -c "ulimit -a"

# Check 
available disk space (small root EBS volumes are common on AWS)
df -h
docker 
system df
```

---

## Short-Term Fix (no reboot required — implement 
immediately)

Add `ENV XZ_OPT="--memlimit=512MiB"` to the `php8med` 
Dockerfile **before** the `apt-get` RUN step. This caps the xz decompressor's 
memory usage and bypasses the allocation failure:

```dockerfile
ENV 
XZ_OPT="--memlimit=512MiB"
```

Then rebuild:

```bash
docker-compose 
build --no-cache php8med
```

---

## Medium-Term Fix

If diagnostics 
reveal restrictive ulimits in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, relax or remove them 
and restart the Docker daemon:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart 
docker
```

---

## Long-Term Fix (recommended)

Ubuntu 16.04 has been 
EOL since April 2021. As tamar1 is an AWS EC2 instance, the correct long-term 
fix is to **replace it with a new instance** based on a current AMI (Ubuntu 
22.04 LTS or 24.04 LTS). Newer kernels have full cgroup v2 support, updated 
Docker compatibility, and this entire class of build problem does not 
occur.

This should be planned as a proper infrastructure upgrade task.
